domain_restrictions: n is an integer greater than 1
m is an integer satisfying 0 less than or equal to m less than or equal to n minus 1
k is an integer summation index with 1 less than or equal to k less than or equal to n
floor argument uses real division of k times m by n (so the input to floor is well-defined as a real number)
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every integer n greater than 1 and every integer m with 0 less than or equal to m less than or equal to n minus 1, if H_n equals the sum from k=1 to n of 1 divided by k and S(n,m) equals the sum from k=1 to n of floor(k*m divided by n) divided by k, then the real inequality m minus S(n,m) is less than or equal to H_n minus 1 holds; moreover, m minus S(n,m) equals H_n minus 1 if and only if m equals n minus 1.
quantifier_order: for all integers n greater than 1
for all integers m with 0 less than or equal to m less than or equal to n minus 1

variables.name: n
variables.role: parameter with restriction n greater than 1; index of the sums

variables.name: k
variables.role: dummy summation index ranging from 1 to n

variables.name: m
variables.role: quantified variable constrained by 0 less than or equal to m less than or equal to n-1

variables.name: H_n
variables.role: derived quantity defined from n by H_n equals sum from k=1 to n of 1 divided by k

variables.name: floor
variables.role: used as floor of k times m divided by n

witness_dependencies: the sum term depends on both n and m through floor(k*m/n)
the equality condition depends on n and m only via whether m equals n minus 1 (no additional existential witnesses are introduced)

statement_nl: Let n be an integer greater than 1, and define H_n = sum_{k=1}^{n} 1/k. For every integer m with 0 <= m <= n-1, m - sum_{k=1}^{n} floor(k m/n)/k <= H_n - 1, and equality holds if and only if m = n-1.
